Hook slide: Why won't my thread stop? Java volatile explained.
Thread A sets running to false, Thread B may still see true, so the loop may never end.
Code: a plain boolean running flag read in a while loop may never see the change.
Code: declare the flag as volatile boolean running so every write is visible to every thread.
Code: volatile int count with count++ is read, add, write. Two threads can overlap and lose updates.
Code: use AtomicInteger and incrementAndGet for atomic updates, or use synchronized.
Recap: flags use volatile, counters use Atomic. volatile means visibility, not mutual exclusion.
